name: Terrain Viewer
description: 3D view of a map's terrain (war3map.w3e): ground textures, heights, water, and where doodads and units are placed.

mcpTools.name: replace_objects
mcpTools.description: Swaps placed objects for other types where they stand, as one edit, such as one tileset's trees for another's: find fitting ones with list_objects, scope game, trees true, tileset map. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes it all back.

kind.description: Default doodads, which also means destructables.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

mcpTools.name: find_pockets
mcpTools.description: Finds walkable ground a unit can't reach from the rest of the map: a sealed gate, a pasture cut in two. Use it after building, instead of testing spots one by one.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

smallest.description: Leave out pockets of fewer pathing cells (32 wide), default 16.

mcpTools.name: check_route
mcpTools.description: Tests a whole road in one call: whether a unit can follow the points in order while staying within a corridor around them. It fails if the only way round leaves the road. Gives the narrowest place and what stands next to it.

points.description: [[x, y], ...], at least two, in order.

mcpTools.name: fill_rows
mcpTools.description: Fills an area with rows of one object, for fields, orchards and lanterns, as one edit. Reserved areas are left free. It reports what didn't fit, like place_objects. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes it all back.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

jitter.description: Up to this far off the grid, default 0.

seed.description: The same number gives the same result, so a tested layout can be made again. The answer says which was used.

mcpTools.name: reserve_area
mcpTools.description: Keeps a place free from now on: scatter_objects and fill_rows leave it out by themselves, in later sessions too. For gates, roads and yards. Kept with the project, and not an edit, so release_area removes it. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

points.description: A path instead of an area: [[x, y], ...], with width.

mcpTools.name: release_area
mcpTools.description: Frees a place reserved with reserve_area. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools.

mcpTools.name: list_reserved_areas
mcpTools.description: The places kept free with reserve_area.

mcpTools.name: list_ground_tiles
mcpTools.description: The game's ground tiles and which tilesets have them, also those the map doesn't use yet. paint_terrain and paint_path take any of them, from any tileset, and add it to the map themselves while it has fewer than 16.

filter.description: Part of an id or a tileset's name, like Village.

mcpTools.name: set_tileset
mcpTools.description: Changes the map's tileset. By default its ground tiles become the new tileset's, slot by slot, so painted ground keeps its pattern; tiles from other tilesets stay. Placed trees don't change: use replace_objects. Use dryRun to see the result, and tell the user, before asking. The user has to confirm it in Studio, within about 90 seconds, so tell them to look there first. It takes a checkpoint first, and undo_last_edit can't take it back. Refused while anything is unsaved. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools.

tileset.description: A letter, like L or A; terrain_info lists them.

replaceTiles.description: Default true. False keeps the ground tiles.

dryRun.description: Change nothing and ask nothing, only report what would happen.

mcpTools.name: resize_map
mcpTools.description: Changes the map's size, side by side, in tiles; objects outside the new map are removed. Use dryRun to see the result, and tell the user, before asking. The user has to confirm it in Studio, within about 90 seconds, so tell them to look there first. It takes a checkpoint first, and undo_last_edit can't take it back. Refused while anything is unsaved. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools.

left.description: Tiles to add to this side, negative to cut. Sizes go in steps of 32, from 32 to 480.

border.description: New widths of the unplayable border: [left, right, bottom, top]. Default: as they are.

dryRun.description: Change nothing and ask nothing, only report what would happen.

mcpTools.name: place_line
mcpTools.description: Places a row along a line, as one edit, for fences and walls: evenly spaced and turned to follow the line. Spacing defaults to the object's footprint. It reports what didn't fit, like place_objects. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes it all back.

spacing.description: Distance between objects. A fence piece is about 190 long.

facingOffset.description: Facing that makes the model follow the line, default 90.

mcpTools.name: check_path
mcpTools.description: Tests whether a unit can walk from one place to another, past cliffs, water, doodads and trees: the length and route of the shortest way for that size, its narrowest place, and how wide the widest way is. If it fails: how far the unit gets, and what size would fit. A close stand-in for the game's pathing, not the game itself. Use it after building something a unit must get through.

from.description: [x, y], or the name of a region (its middle).

to.description: [x, y], or the name of a region (its middle).

unitSize.description: Collision size, default 32. Most units are 16 to 48.

mcpTools.name: paint_path
mcpTools.description: Paints a trail along points, as one edit, frayed along its sides and at its ends. With flatten it also levels the ground across it. Keep it free with avoid in scatter_objects, using the same points, and test it with check_path.

points.description: [[x, y], ...], at least two, in order.

edge.description: 0 to 1, default 0.4: how much of the sides thins out.

seed.description: The same number gives the same result, so a tested layout can be made again. The answer says which was used.

mcpTools.name: paint_terrain
mcpTools.description: Paints ground tiles over a region or rectangle, as one edit. Any of the game's tiles works, from any tileset: list_ground_tiles has them, and a new one joins the map's list by itself. Layer several for a natural look: a wide patch, then smaller ones on top. Objects on it follow the ground; pathing, shadows and the minimap are rebuilt. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes it all back.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

edge.description: 0 to 1, default 0.3: how much of the outside thins out, so the patch has no clean border.

seed.description: The same number gives the same result, so a tested layout can be made again. The answer says which was used.

mcpTools.name: sculpt_terrain
mcpTools.description: Reshapes the ground in a region or rectangle, as one edit: strongest in the middle, fading to nothing at the edge, so it makes no steps. It doesn't make cliffs. Call it several times for several hills. Objects on it follow the ground; pathing, shadows and the minimap are rebuilt. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes it all back.

amount.description: raise and lower: height in world units, default 64, at most 1000. flatten: the height to go to, default the area's average. A unit is about 64 tall.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

mcpTools.name: place_objects
mcpTools.description: Places units, items, doodads or destructables at given points, on the ground, as one edit. Doodads get a random variation, facing and size unless given. It reports each object that didn't fit and why. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes all of it back at once.

kind.description: units also means items; doodads also means destructables, such as trees.

ignoreRoom.description: Place even where something is in the way.

seed.description: The same number gives the same result, so a tested layout can be made again. The answer says which was used.

nearest.description: Where there's no room, use the nearest free spot within 320, and say so.

dryRun.description: Change nothing, only report what would fit.

mcpTools.name: scatter_objects
mcpTools.description: Fills a region or rectangle with doodads or destructables, like the editor's Scatter brush: spaced by their size, with random types from ids, variation, facing and size, on free ground only. For forests, rocks, grass. As one edit. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes all of it back at once.

kind.description: units also means items; doodads also means destructables, such as trees.

ids.description: Types to mix, like ATtr. Find them with list_objects, scope game, tileset map.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

density.description: 0.05 to 1, default 0.7. 1 packs them as close as they fit.

seed.description: The same number gives the same result, so a tested layout can be made again. The answer says which was used.

scaleRange.description: [smallest, biggest] size, instead of what the type picks. Small ones keep mushrooms and flowers modest.

shape.description: ellipse (default) thins out towards a natural edge; box fills the rectangle.

avoid.description: Places to keep free: {region}, a rectangle, or a path as {points, width}.

mcpTools.name: move_object
mcpTools.description: Moves a placed object, following the ground. index and id come from list_placed. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes all of it back at once.

kind.description: units also means items; doodads also means destructables, such as trees.

mcpTools.name: remove_objects
mcpTools.description: Removes placed objects: those listed by index and id from list_placed, or all matching an area with id or player. Without either it does nothing. Needs the setting mcp.writeTools; undo_last_edit takes all of it back at once.

kind.description: units also means items; doodads also means destructables, such as trees.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

mcpTools.name: terrain_info
mcpTools.description: The ground of a region or rectangle, or the whole map: heights, cliff levels, ground tiles in use and the tileset's others, water, and a text map of where things can stand, including what stands there now. Use before placing.

heights.description: Also give the ground heights as rows of numbers from the north.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

mcpTools.name: terrain_screenshot
mcpTools.description: A picture of the open map in the terrain editor's 3D view, with its doodads and units, however the user has set up their own view. With a region or rectangle it looks at that place, outlined with its coordinates, north up; without one it shows from the user's camera. Use it to check your work.

view.description: For an area: from above (default), at the editor's angle, or low, which shows hills against the sky.

overlay.description: pathing: red where units can't walk, orange where something stands, blue for water. heights: blue (low) to red (high), with a line every 32 units.

region.description: A region of the map, by name.

services.description: Tool groups (tabs) in the terrain editor: registerToolGroup.

terrain.animate.description: Placed objects play their Stand animation in the terrain view (off: they stand still).

terrain.lighting.enabled.description: Light the terrain view with the map's day/night lighting (off: an even light, e.g. when the map's lighting is very dark).

terrain.lighting.hour.description: Hour of the game day the terrain view is lit at.

terrain.pathing.regenerate.description: Rewrite the pathing map (war3map.wpm) from terrain and doodads on every save.

terrain.pathing.deepWater.description: Water deeper than this (world units, at a cell's nearest corner) can't be walked. 52 matches the World Editor.

terrain.shadows.update.description: Update the shadow map (war3map.shd) on save. Only cells whose predicted shadow changed since the last save are rewritten.

terrain.shadows.sunAzimuth.description: Direction toward the sun in degrees, counter-clockwise from east (225 = south-west, as the World Editor).

terrain.shadows.sunElevation.description: Sun height above the horizon in degrees (30 as the World Editor). Lower casts longer shadows.

terrain.minimap.regenerate.description: When to redraw the minimap (war3mapMap.blp). "After edits" keeps the World Editor's image until something changes.

terrain.minimap.groundBrightness.description: Ground colour relative to the average colour of its texture.

terrain.minimap.waterShallowColor.description: Water colour [r, g, b] at shallow depth (for Lordaeron water; other tilesets are shifted toward their own minimap water colour).

terrain.minimap.waterDeepColor.description: Water colour [r, g, b] at full depth.

terrain.minimap.waterOpacityShallow.description: How much shallow water covers the ground (0–1).

terrain.minimap.waterOpacityDeep.description: How much deep water covers the ground (0–1).

terrain.minimap.waterFullDepth.description: Depth (world units) at which water reaches its deep colour and opacity.

terrain.minimap.objectRadius.description: Size of tree/doodad dots (in tiles) for objects with a minimap colour.

terrain.minimap.blurPasses.description: Softening passes (the World Editor's minimaps are soft).

terrain.minimap.jpegQuality.description: JPEG quality of the minimap file.
